_why: Skill-candidates row 'commit the BashParse false-proof sweep as a test' (2486). The sweep's property: wherever bash runs an operator, the oracle proves it literal nowhere. Each row restores a soundness regression a review round found, and must be caught by the SWEEP rather than by its hand-written pin.

mutations.name: sweep-sees-a-probe-proved-without-its-control
mutations._mechanism: R13 restored: a probe that breaks the parse proves the quote alone, though after `}` any quoted word breaks it. The sweep's `{ :; } @ b` lines turn up as false proofs.
mutations.find: return self._parses(probe) is False and self._parses(control) is True  # M:ORACLE-PROVES

mutations.name: sweep-sees-a-probe-after-a-live-backslash
mutations._mechanism: R14 restored: after a live backslash the payload joins the heredoc delimiter (`<<E\ 'x'` is `E x`), so a code `&&` is proven quoted. Caught through the sweep's `{ cat <<E\@ b` / `E x` / `E&` frame.

mutations.name: sweep-sees-a-body-line-proved-without-the-line-check
mutations._mechanism: Drops the doubled-operator line check before the body probe, so a line under a fake heredoc header (`echo '<<E'`) that bash RUNS is proven literal.
